patches.value: For every tau>0 and positive integer Lsrc, consider the uniform grid t_jsrc=j*tau, jsrc=0,...,Lsrc, on [0,Lsrc*tau]. For every integer nsrc with 0<=nsrc<Lsrc, put a=t_nsrc=nsrc*tau. In particular nsrc=0 is an admissible step for every tau>0, with a=t_0=0 and t_1=tau. For 0<sigma<=1, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero f,g in H^sigma, the source bilinear stage F_a(t;f,g) satisfies ||F_a(t;f,g)||_(H^beta)<=C*tau^((1+sigma-beta)/(1+sigma-beta0))*||f||_(H^sigma)*||g||_(H^sigma) for every beta in [beta0,1+sigma]. Here beta0=2*sigma-3/2 if 0<sigma<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 if sigma=1/2, and beta0=sigma-1 if 1/2<sigma<=1. Norms in this source assertion are unnormalized; C can depend on sigma and on a fixed epsilon, but not on tau, nsrc, Lsrc or spectral support. The grid horizon Lsrc*tau is auxiliary and need not equal the problem parameter T.

value.context: Sections 1-2 and 3.3: 2*pi-periodic functions, coefficients normalized by 1/(2*pi) but function norms use unnormalized dx; P deletes zero mode. Interval endpoints nonnegative, length bounded by a fixed constant. Source estimates are uniform in time level, timestep and spectral support. The source convergence theorem is not imported. The grid is explicitly t_n=n*tau, n=0,...,L, tau=T/L (p.4; repeated p.20). Lemma 7.2 applies to every step 0<=n<L, including n=0. For an arbitrary positive tau, take the auxiliary source horizon Lsrc*tau with any positive integer Lsrc (in particular Lsrc=1); this gives an admissible source base zero without an extra premise. Equations (7.2)-(7.3) define its time-independent mean-zero bilinear stage; the proof on pp.33-34 derives bounds from integrals of length at most tau and endpoint norm bounds, without a solution or convergence hypothesis.
